title: SET BOUNDARIES
mv: Have you found honey? Eat only as much as you need, Lest you be filled with it and vomit.
mvp: “Have you found honey? Eat only as much as you need, Lest you be filled with it and vomit.” Proverbs 25:16 (NKJV)
assignment: Write down five (5) key areas of your life where you need to set (or reinforce) boundaries (2X5=10 marks).

b.x: A boundary is a restriction that indicates one cannot go beyond a particular margin. To set boundaries is to establish limits in your relationships and dealings to protect your mental health and overall well-being. Boundaries can be relational, emotional, intellectual, physical, official, time-related, etc. Setting boundaries will include clearly defined behaviours and interactions you find acceptable and unacceptable, and communicating these limits to others. Be truthful and consistent to enforce your boundaries and never entertain any guilt for setting boundaries to protect yourself.
There are different types of boundaries, but we shall limit ourselves to the following.

i: Physical Boundary: You firmly say no to unwanted physical touch and invasion of your personal space. It also includes limits on food and rest to protect your welfare (Genesis 39:7-9, 12; Proverbs 23:19-21).
Emotional Boundary: You do not allow others to quash your feelings or share your personal information without prior permission from you (Galatians 5:22-23).

Time Boundary: This is when you limit the amount of time you spend on work to avoid burnout. It also extends to time spent with people who are good at wasting your precious time with unnecessary engagements (Ephesians 5:16-17; Luke 5:16).

Weak Boundary: These are boundaries set with weak rules which are easily broken by the parties involved (Hosea 5:10). The parties are not truthful to each other, and they often say ‘Yes’ to what they should say ‘No’ to. The boundaries are often not set with clarity.

Rigid Boundary: These boundaries are more of laws than guidance. It denies an enriched relationship. Others are regarded as suspects, and in a bid to protect your privacy, you end up being lonely as everyone is kept at needless arm’s length.

Healthy Boundary: This is a flexible boundary based on mutual agreement without any iota of fear or duress. It is not set in fear because each party in the agreement knows what is expected of them and is familiar with their goals and aspirations before setting the boundaries. It is often set under God’s guidance (Isaiah 58:11).

b.x: Setting boundaries in relationships, at the workplace, in families, etc., is important (Mark 1:35). Boundaries help people to know their limits and that they cannot push past them. Nobody takes you for granted at your workplace or anywhere else. With time, people get to respect your boundaries and respect you in return because they already know what you can tolerate. Boundaries help you to know what to say and how and when to say it (Matthew 5:37). It guides you to where to go and where not to go (Proverbs 25:17). It helps with your association, and you know who to walk with and who to stay away from (Proverbs 13:20). Boundaries serve as a caution to guide from making errors (Proverbs 22:3). You also avoid stress, and burnout by protecting your time, energy, and emotional space (Matthew 14:23). Setting boundaries build trust, respect, safe and good relationships and keeps your emotional and mental health (Isaiah 26:3).
Setting boundaries helps build a wall of protection around you and ward off intruders.
